title: Arkret Seal
description: A final certificate for one Realm safety domain. It confirms the ordered outcomes of registered security commands. Ordinary data has no covering Seal. Canonical signing bytes are RFC8785 JSON of every top-level field except id and notary_signature; id is derived from those bytes. A quorum certificate is valid only under the exact predecessor configuration and its durable consensus rules.

id.description: Content-derived typed reference. hex part MUST equal H(seal_canonical_bytes) under the Realm digest_algorithm, where seal_canonical_bytes is the canonical JSON of every signed body field EXCEPT `id` and `notary_signature`. Receivers MUST recompute and verify; mismatch → digest_mismatch. NEVER include `id` in the hash input — that would create a self-reference.

realm_id.description: The safety domain identifier. v1 has exactly one confirmed safety sequence per Realm. Circle, MLS and other safety resources within it share this sequence; ordinary data does not participate.

predecessor_ref.description: Null only at the registered atomic genesis; every successor names exactly one confirmed predecessor in the same Realm. A Seal never joins competing safety branches.

delta.description: Canonical sorted unique union of successful security Event digests from committed command_result units. Registered atomic bootstrap data members share the unit outcome but are not included in delta. Failed commands and standalone ordinary data are excluded.

control_event_set_root.description: Authenticated root over the recursive covered_set of this Seal. Default construction is RFC6962 Merkle root over canonical bytewise-sorted covered_set(S); inclusion uses Merkle audit path and non-membership uses sorted-neighbor proof. The root is not computed over delta[] alone.

state_root.description: RFC6962 authenticated root of all written sequenced_state cells in this Realm. Each leaf is JCS({cell:CellRef,state:{revision_event_id:EventId,value:complete_registered_value}}), sorted by CellRef code point. It excludes ordinary cells. Command outcomes and auxiliary certificates are directly committed by the signed Seal body.

notary_seq.description: Unique monotonically increasing confirmed position within this Realm lineage; genesis is zero. The sole authority must durably refuse a second distinct body at the same position.

availability_receipt_digests.description: Canonical bytewise-sorted, duplicate-free full canonical content digests of every and only AvailabilityReceipt required for this Seal's delta admission. Empty when no receipt is required. The receiver resolves every digest through the registered governance-dependency surface and verifies the full signed receipt; missing or surplus receipts reject the Seal. This list replaces the redundant availability_root.

covered_event_digests.description: Optional compaction materialization of the full recursive covered_set(S), canonical bytewise-sorted and duplicate-free. When present, receivers MUST verify it equals set(delta) union all predecessor covered sets and that control_event_set_root is computed over this exact set. Non-compaction Seals normally omit it.

previous_state_root.description: Hash-algorithm transition only: present iff this Seal is a Transition Seal under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1. It commits the governance view before the transition Move is applied, computed with previous_digest_algorithm. state_root commits the post-transition governance view with the new suite. See event-auth-state-resolution.md §13.

previous_digest_algorithm.description: Canonical active digest-suite id used for previous_state_root. Required iff previous_state_root is present, absent on non-transition Seals, and byte-equal to the transition Move from_digest_algorithm. A profile id is invalid here.

notary_signature.description: The sole configured authority signs JCS({context:"ak.seal.commit.v1",seal_digest}); seal_digest authenticates the complete canonical unsigned Seal body, including Realm, configuration, sequence, predecessor and results.

sealed_at.description: Monotone signed safety-decision timestamp, at least the predecessor timestamp. Not an ordinary Event arrival order or authorization freshness lease. Finite existence anchors additionally require the bounded-clock prepare evidence defined by cbs-profiles.md. Excess future skew is deferred, not a permanent competing finality decision.

configuration_ref.description: The exact accepted realm.create or realm.notary command that installed the signing configuration. Genesis uses its own realm.create Event identity, never a future Seal identity.

command_results.description: Confirmed order of atomic command units, including rejected outcomes. Each Event digest appears in exactly one unit. A unit is all-or-nothing; no prefix of a rejected unit has effects.

authorization_closures.description: Exactly the closures derived from successful revocation/lifecycle commands in this Seal. Entries cannot be added by notary discretion. Ordinary data does not wait for this field or for new Seals.

existence_anchors.description: Optional, explicitly finite-authorization existence evidence. Every included Event and ancestor is fully available and verified before prepare. Its safe existence interval is sealed_at +/- 2*configuration.max_clock_error_ms. The entire interval must lie in the exact authorization window. It is not a lease for unbounded ordinary data.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key. Bare DID is not valid for signatures because verifiers need a stable verification method, not only a controller DID.

payload_digest.description: Hash of the complete enclosing phase transcript, including its domain separator and coordinates; never the raw Seal body digest.

signature.description: One canonical JWS from the exact frozen authority. The protected alg and kid match the descriptor; payload_digest is the digest of the domain-separated commit or read-proof transcript, never an alternative authority. Reject noncanonical encoding and unknown critical headers.

result_digest.description: H(JCS({event_digest,unit_event_digests,outcome,effects,reason_code})). effects is the unique CellRef-sorted array of {cell_id,state}, one complete final post-unit state per touched Cell after all registered writes in their normative order. A rejected unit has effects=[] and the exact registered reason_code; a committed unit uses reason_code=null. Only registered atomic units may combine Events. Recompute from original Events at the execution position, never from HTTP output. The exact preimage shape is $defs/command_result_digest_input; each effect state uses the canonical family model, including complete ordinary causal coverage and set tombstones.

reason_code.description: Required only for rejected outcomes. It must be the registered reason deterministically produced by execution of this command at this sequence position; arbitrary or unknown reasons are invalid.

unit_event_digests.description: Exact execution-ordered members of the registered atomic command unit. A standalone command is [event_digest]. A registered bootstrap/cascade uses its normative order and first member as event_digest; arbitrary batching cannot create a unit. Each Event belongs to at most one result in the entire confirmed history.

scope_ref.description: Scope of the verified authorization dependency being closed, not the ordinary Event's resource scope. Device and Agent key dependencies use their bound PCR scope even when used in another Realm; resource selector coverage and authorization remain independently required. Derive this coordinate from the verified authorization source, never from an unverified Event assertion.

state.description: The complete post-unit state selected by the canonical Cell family state_model, with exactly the corresponding snapshot state shape. In particular causal_register retains covered_event_ids and heads; bootstrap ordinary state is never converted into sequenced_state or a display value. The family fixes the model; the producer cannot select another matching branch.

unit_event_digests.description: Exact execution-ordered members of the registered atomic command unit. A standalone command is [event_digest]. A registered bootstrap/cascade uses its normative order and first member as event_digest; arbitrary batching cannot create a unit. Each Event belongs to at most one result in the entire confirmed history.

effects.description: Strict CellRef order, exactly one complete final state for every Cell touched by the unit.
